seen_animation: A tall flask-shaped vase (wide flat lip, narrow curved neck, flaring body, open gap at the lower left of the base) stands in the frame with a scribbled hand entering from the lower left and resting its fingers (drawn as a '3'-like stack of loops) against the left side of the body. Across frames 1-16 the vase outline and the hand stay in place while the painted marks on the body slide from left to right: in frames 1-4 a leaf mark sits near the left and an oval with an inner loop sits near the right edge; in frames 5-8 both drift right and the right oval starts to flatten against the right contour; in frames 9-12 a new oval appears from behind the hand at the left edge and the right oval becomes a thin sliver at the contour; in frames 13-16 the right sliver has gone, and the new left oval and the leaf have moved toward the middle of the body. It reads as the vase turning on its axis while the hand steadies it.
seen_film: A wide painted pottery bowl on a low foot is shown close up, with a person's hand at the lower left touching the bowl near the base. The bowl rotates: in frames 1-8 a large round medallion with a teardrop inside sits at the right side and moves right toward the edge, leaf and diamond patterns pass across the middle; in frames 9-12 the medallion is compressed at the right edge and leaves the view; in frames 9-16 a new medallion enters from the left edge and by frames 13-16 it sits at the left third of the bowl. The hand stays in roughly the same place with small finger shifts. The camera does not move.
named_subject: A flask-shaped vase (the doodle) being turned on its axis, steadied by a hand, its painted marks rotating around the body.
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. e.png 1-16: the leaf and right oval drift right a few pixels per frame and the right oval flattens to a sliver against the right contour, matching f.png 1-16 where the right medallion moves toward the right edge and compresses. e.png 13-24: a new oval emerges from behind the hand at the left contour as f.png 13-24 brings the new medallion in at the left edge. e.png 25-38: the left oval and leaf continue to the left third/middle and the right sliver is gone, matching f.png 25-38 where the medallion settles at the left third. g.png shows the marks as one continuous left-to-right band with no gaps or reversals. The vase outline and hand stay fixed in every frame, as the bowl and hand do in the film. a.png 1-16 against d.png 1-16: the entry and exit of the large mark land on the same numbered frames (right exit around 9-12, left entry around 9-13).
primary_gap: The vase carries only two or three marks at a time, so the rotation is shown by a sparse set of shapes and the hand barely changes while the film's hand shifts its fingers slightly; the turn reads, but with less visible surface pattern than the film.
closes_when: One additional small mark (for example a second leaf) travels across the body in step with the others between e.png frames 1 and 38, and the finger loops shift by a few pixels around frames 13-20 as the film's fingers do.
protect: The c.png vase silhouette (flat lip, curved neck, flared body, gap at lower left of base) held identically in every frame; the steady left-to-right drift of the marks with foreshortening to a sliver at the right contour and emergence from behind the hand at the left; the timing that matches the film's medallion exit and entry; the fixed hand position.
identity_gap: The vase is the c.png drawing with the same lip, neck curve, body flare and open base corner; the added marks and hand use the same single thin wobbly stroke, so nothing departs from the doodle.
